sources.title: FLEX — Flame Extinguishment Experiment — approach
sources.text: The FLEX experiments involve igniting and observing the burning behavior of relatively large droplets. A primary objective of the experiments is to determine the Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) as a function of ambient pressure and determine how the presence of a suppressant influences the LOI .

sources.title: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis — approach
sources.text: OpenFOAM was used to develop a 3-D CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier–Stokes flow with low-temperature combustion chemistry, coupled heat and mass transfer, and radiation. Model fidelity was established against ISS FLEX measurements, after which controlled simulations examined three forcing modes (i) convection alone to mimic droplet drift, (ii) imposed heat flux, and (iii) combined convection plus heating applied to both large (1–4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplets.

sources.text: Can cool flames support quasi-steady alkane droplet burning?; Cool-flame extinction during n-alkane droplet combustion in microgravity; Partial-Burning Regime for Quasi-Steady Droplet Combustion Supported by Cool Flames; The role of cool-flame chemistry in quasi-steady combustion and extinction of n-heptane droplets; Asymptotic analysis of quasi-steady n-heptane droplet combustion supported by cool-flame chemistry; Science in Short: Cool Flames; Low Temperature n-Dodecane Droplet Combustion Experiments Aboard the International Space Station

sources.title: STDCE-1 — Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment-1 — approach
More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
sources.text: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption. Limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.

sources.title: FLEX compares CO2 and helium as gaseous suppressants
sources.text: At 21 % O2, share of FLEX tests ending in flame extinction before burnout by atmosphere — N2 only: 14/29; CO2: 13/18; He: 7/7. FLEX varied CO2 up to 0.7 and He up to 0.45 mole fraction. Limitation: Small samples per cell; droplet size and pressure also vary — use the Extract module to control for them.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.
